grasp_geometry_calibration.geometry_basis: Visual mesh vertex bounds of gripper inner/outer link4 relative to the nominal gripper center_link (wrist-local +z is the TCP approach axis; open/close axis is wrist-local x; wrist-local y is the pad width axis). Values are the mesh axis-aligned extents in the author static pose of robot_fix.usda, NOT the PhysX convex-decomposition collision bodies, NOT measured contact surfaces, and passive finger joints (joint3 +/-10 deg, joint4 +/-2 deg) are NOT modeled. Left/right sides differ by less than 5 micrometres; nominal values are rounded. fingertip_beyond_tcp_m is the farthest mesh point beyond the TCP along the approach axis (about 10.3 mm); pad_contact_zone_m spans the finger-pad mesh from about 42.7 mm behind the TCP to 10.3 mm beyond it; pad_width_m is the larger (outer finger) mesh span along the width axis; pad_thickness_m is the per-finger mesh span along the open/close axis in the author pose, which is not the runtime aperture. pad_widths_per_finger_m (added 2026-09-22) is the per-finger pad span along the width axis from the same wrist-frame mesh extraction: the two fingers have EQUAL extent along the approach axis (inner/outer link4 spans 53.2/52.8 mm), so the only significant finger asymmetry is pad WIDTH (outer 60.4 mm vs inner 26 mm); under open/close-axis roll the wider finger's far edge (about 30 mm from the TCP midplane) reaches a surface before the narrower finger's edge (about 13 mm). These bounds do not certify collision-free motion, contact, or grasp success, and vary with gripper orientation and state.
